s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks' duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
No response to 10 days of amoxicillin-clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology and revealed new bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis but no uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation results
No asthenia, headaches, abdominal pain, striae, or buffalo hump

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and associated adrenal gland abnormalities are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT in the right testis suggests a malignant process, and lymphoma is a possible cause

shortlist.label: seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Seminoma is a common testicular tumor that can present with painless swelling and may be associated with adrenal gland abnormalities

shortlist.label: adrenal myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement is consistent with this diagnosis, although the absence of uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT is unusual

shortlist.label: adrenocortical adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Adrenal gland abnormalities and the absence of systemic symptoms are consistent with a non-functioning adrenal adenoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painless testicular swelling and the ultrasound findings of testicular enlargement and inhomogeneity, along with the intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT, are consistent with a testicular tumor. Leydig cell tumor is a type of testicular tumor that can present with these features, and the absence of systemic symptoms and normal laboratory results also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would likely show systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: seminoma
rejected.why: Seminoma is a type of testicular cancer, but it is more common in younger men and often presents with testicular pain and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: adrenal myelolipoma
rejected.why: Adrenal myelolipoma is a benign tumor of the adrenal gland, but it does not explain the testicular findings in this case.

rejected.label: adrenocortical adenoma
rejected.why: Adrenocortical adenoma is a tumor of the adrenal gland, but it does not explain the testicular findings and the intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT in the testis.
